gen-fs-styro-gf-athiti: Approachable and contemporary, Athiti draws each line like cut vinyl. Styro, by contrast, crowds its letters tight and swells with retro command, so a long page of Athiti feels open and easy to move through.
gen-fs-styro-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible: Styro packs its retro, commanding letters tightly, with e and c nearly sealed shut against the white around them. Atkinson Hyperlegible sans opens every s wide, so a long passage moves along without a snag.
gen-fs-styro-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible-mo: Crowded, nearly sealed letters give Styro its retro punch. Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono is the opposite, with sans spacing stretched wide and counters that let a long stretch of text breathe.
gen-fs-styro-gf-biryani: Retro and tightly packed, with barely a gap in its letters. Biryani is the release: a plain sans whose curves are as heavy as its stems, with big open eyes that keep everything clear.
gen-fs-styro-gf-blinker: Blinker brings lowercase that fills most of its height and holds its lines steady. Styro handles the loud, retro, tightly packed statement, while Blinker handles the clear, open reading that follows.
gen-fs-styro-gf-carrois-gothic: Styro's crowded, nearly closed e and c give it a retro, commanding look that reads like a stamp. It earns its keep big and short, leaving Carrois Gothic to quieter work.
gen-fs-styro-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Carrois Gothic SC keeps capitals and lowercase nearly level and leaves every curve clearly open, against Styro's crowded retro heading. Over a long stretch it reads smoothly and without fuss.
gen-fs-styro-gf-cascadia-code: Tight, retro and commanding up top, then a wire-thin sans-serif below. Cascadia Code uses one unchanging pen and wide spacing, and that gap against Styro's crowded letters is the pair's real hook.
gen-fs-styro-gf-cascadia-mono: Tight, crowded and retro, Styro leads with command, with its e and c nearly shut. And Cascadia Mono, a plain sans with rod-stock strokes, stands its letters like pins in a wide board, quietly open.
